questions.prompt: Which statement best describes Business Studies?
options: The study of activities involved in producing, distributing, and using goods and services
The study of only plants and animals in the environment
The study of drawing maps and locating mountains
The study of only games played during school sports
questions.correctAnswer: The study of activities involved in producing, distributing, and using goods and services
questions.explanation: Business Studies helps learners understand how goods and services are produced, distributed, consumed, recorded, and managed.
questions.learningOutcome: Examine the concept of Business Studies in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which component of Business Studies deals with keeping business transaction records?
options: Accounting
Meteorology
Drama
Geography
questions.correctAnswer: Accounting
questions.explanation: Accounting involves recording and summarising business transactions so that decisions can be made using reliable information.
questions.learningOutcome: Examine the components of Business Studies in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which career is directly related to Business Studies?
options: Accountant
Goalkeeper
Rainmaker
Mountain climber
questions.correctAnswer: Accountant
questions.explanation: An accountant uses business knowledge to prepare, check, and interpret financial records.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore career opportunities related to Business Studies in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Why is learning Business Studies useful in day-to-day life?
options: It helps people make informed buying, selling, saving, and earning decisions
It stops people from needing goods and services
It teaches learners to avoid all work
It replaces every other school subject
questions.correctAnswer: It helps people make informed buying, selling, saving, and earning decisions
questions.explanation: Business knowledge supports practical choices about money, work, enterprise, and consumption.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the importance of Business Studies in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to start a small beadwork enterprise after school. Which Business Studies area would help most?
options: Entrepreneurship
Weather recording
Music notation
Food digestion
questions.correctAnswer: Entrepreneurship
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship focuses on identifying business opportunities and organising resources to start and run a business.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate Business Studies knowledge to career and enterprise opportunities.

questions.prompt: What is the main use of money in buying goods and services?
options: It acts as a medium of exchange
It grows crops by itself
It prevents communication
It removes all human wants
questions.correctAnswer: It acts as a medium of exchange
questions.explanation: Money is generally accepted in exchange for goods and services, making trade easier than barter.
questions.learningOutcome: Illustrate the uses of money in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Which example shows money being used as a store of value?
options: Saving part of pocket money in a bank account
Throwing coins into a river
Refusing to compare prices
Giving away all receipts immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Saving part of pocket money in a bank account
questions.explanation: Money can store value when it is saved for future use instead of being spent immediately.
questions.learningOutcome: Illustrate the uses of money in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Which feature helps users identify a genuine Kenya currency note?
options: Security thread
Loose exercise page
Ordinary pencil mark
School timetable
questions.correctAnswer: Security thread
questions.explanation: Security features such as a security thread, watermark, serial number, and raised print make genuine notes harder to copy.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the key security features of the Kenyan currency.

questions.prompt: Why should traders check the security features on currency notes?
options: To reduce the risk of accepting counterfeit money
To make customers wait for no reason
To stop legal buying and selling
To change the value printed on the note
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce the risk of accepting counterfeit money
questions.explanation: Checking security features protects the trader, customer, and economy from fake currency.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the key security features of the Kenyan currency.

questions.prompt: What do themes and symbols on Kenyan currency mainly help citizens recognise?
options: National heritage, resources, and identity
Private passwords of bank customers
The daily price of every item
The exact profit of every shop
questions.correctAnswer: National heritage, resources, and identity
questions.explanation: Currency symbols and images can communicate national identity, heritage, and economic activities.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe themes and symbols on the Kenyan currency.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains a personal goal?
options: A target a person wants to achieve within a given time
A random item bought without planning
A rule that bans all saving
A mistake made in a receipt
questions.correctAnswer: A target a person wants to achieve within a given time
questions.explanation: A personal goal gives direction because it states what someone wants to achieve and guides effort toward it.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore the meaning and importance of setting personal goals for self-development.

questions.prompt: Which personal goal is written most clearly?
options: Save 200 shillings by the end of four weeks
Become better someday
Do many things later
Spend money whenever I see snacks
questions.correctAnswer: Save 200 shillings by the end of four weeks
questions.explanation: A clear goal states the amount, action, and time frame, making progress easier to track.
questions.learningOutcome: Set personal goals for self-development.

questions.prompt: Why is time an important factor when setting a personal goal?
options: It helps a learner know when to review progress
It removes the need to make effort
It makes the goal secret
It changes wants into needs automatically
questions.correctAnswer: It helps a learner know when to review progress
questions.explanation: A time frame supports planning, monitoring, and adjusting action toward a goal.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the factors to consider when setting personal goals for self-development.

questions.prompt: A learner sets a goal to improve handwriting by practising for 15 minutes daily. Which factor is shown?
options: Commitment to regular action
Avoiding all feedback
Ignoring time completely
Choosing without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Commitment to regular action
questions.explanation: Regular practice shows commitment, which is important when working toward self-development goals.
questions.learningOutcome: Use personal goals for self-development.

questions.prompt: Which tool can help a learner track progress toward a savings goal?
options: A simple savings record in an exercise book
A blank wall with no notes
A torn receipt thrown away
A closed shop sign
questions.correctAnswer: A simple savings record in an exercise book
questions.explanation: Writing savings entries helps the learner monitor progress and make better money decisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Use ICT devices or exercise books for setting personal goals for self-development.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes a talent from an ability?
options: A talent is a natural strength, while an ability can be developed through learning and practice
A talent is always bought from a shop, while an ability is always a coin
A talent belongs only to adults, while an ability belongs only to businesses
A talent is a receipt, while an ability is a tax
questions.correctAnswer: A talent is a natural strength, while an ability can be developed through learning and practice
questions.explanation: Talents are natural strengths, but abilities can grow through training, practice, feedback, and experience.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between talents and abilities of learners in school.

questions.prompt: Which activity can nurture a learner's baking talent for business purposes?
options: Practising recipes, getting feedback, and learning safe food handling
Hiding all ingredients from the teacher
Selling food without hygiene
Refusing to compare costs
questions.correctAnswer: Practising recipes, getting feedback, and learning safe food handling
questions.explanation: Practice, feedback, safety, and cost awareness help a talent become useful for enterprise.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ways of nurturing talents and abilities for business purpose.

questions.prompt: Which example shows an ethical use of talent in business?
options: Designing posters for a club and charging the agreed price
Copying another learner's design and selling it as your own
Cheating customers about the quality of a product
Using skill to overcharge younger learners
questions.correctAnswer: Designing posters for a club and charging the agreed price
questions.explanation: Ethical use of talent requires honesty, respect for other people's work, and fair treatment of customers.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ethical issues related to the use of talents and abilities in business.

questions.prompt: A learner is good at public speaking. Which career opportunity connects well with that ability?
options: Sales representative
Silent stone carver only
Closed shop guard only
Currency printer only
questions.correctAnswer: Sales representative
questions.explanation: Sales representatives often use communication skills to explain products and persuade customers honestly.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate talents and abilities to career opportunities in the world.

questions.prompt: Why can nurturing talents and abilities help generate income?
options: Improved skills can be used to provide valuable goods or services
Talents always remove all business costs
Abilities make customers buy without choice
Skills stop the need for honesty
questions.correctAnswer: Improved skills can be used to provide valuable goods or services
questions.explanation: Well-developed skills can help a person produce goods or provide services that other people are willing to pay for.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the importance of nurturing talent and abilities in generating income.

questions.prompt: Which item is a human need rather than a want?
options: Clean drinking water
A second pair of luxury headphones
A decorative phone cover
A video game subscription
questions.correctAnswer: Clean drinking water
questions.explanation: Needs are things required for survival or basic well-being, while wants make life more comfortable but are not essential.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between needs and wants as used in Business Studies.

questions.prompt: What does scarcity mean in Business Studies?
options: Available resources are not enough to satisfy all human wants
People have no wants at all
All goods are free and unlimited
Every choice has no effect
questions.correctAnswer: Available resources are not enough to satisfy all human wants
questions.explanation: Scarcity exists because human wants are many while resources such as money, time, labour, and materials are limited.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore scarcity in relation to satisfaction of consumer needs and wants.

questions.prompt: A learner has 100 shillings and chooses lunch instead of a notebook. What is the opportunity cost?
options: The notebook not bought
The lunch already chosen
The school bell
The shopkeeper's counter
questions.correctAnswer: The notebook not bought
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up when a choice is made.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore opportunity cost in relation to satisfaction of consumer needs and wants.

questions.prompt: What is a scale of preference?
options: A list of wants arranged from most important to least important
A receipt showing tax paid
A currency security thread
A poster for a sports day
questions.correctAnswer: A list of wants arranged from most important to least important
questions.explanation: A scale of preference helps a consumer or business rank choices when resources are limited.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore scale of preference in relation to satisfaction of consumer needs and wants.

questions.prompt: Which list is the best scale of preference for a learner preparing for school with limited money?
options: Exercise book, pen, lunch, extra sweets
Extra sweets, toy, second cap, exercise book
Phone cover, party card, pen, food
Decorative sticker, bracelet, snack, ruler
questions.correctAnswer: Exercise book, pen, lunch, extra sweets
questions.explanation: A good scale of preference places essential learning and health needs before less urgent wants.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare a scale of preference to satisfy personal needs and wants.

questions.prompt: Which activity is an example of extraction?
options: Mining stones from a quarry
Baking bread from flour
Selling airtime in a kiosk
Carrying goods to a market
questions.correctAnswer: Mining stones from a quarry
questions.explanation: Extraction involves obtaining resources directly from nature, such as mining, fishing, farming, and quarrying.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse trading and business activities in the community.

questions.prompt: Which activity best shows trading in a local market?
options: Buying tomatoes from a farmer and selling them to consumers
Reading a weather report silently
Planting trees without exchange
Repairing a desk for personal use only
questions.correctAnswer: Buying tomatoes from a farmer and selling them to consumers
questions.explanation: Trading involves buying and selling goods or services, usually with the aim of earning income or profit.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse trading activities in the community.

questions.prompt: Why are business activities important to a community?
options: They provide goods, services, employment, and income
They stop all movement of goods
They remove the need for consumers
They make resources useless
questions.correctAnswer: They provide goods, services, employment, and income
questions.explanation: Business activities help satisfy needs and wants while creating income opportunities for individuals and communities.
questions.learningOutcome: Justify the need for business activities for self and the community.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows the role of a retailer to consumers?
options: Selling goods in small quantities near consumers
Printing all national currency
Making county laws alone
Stopping consumers from comparing prices
questions.correctAnswer: Selling goods in small quantities near consumers
questions.explanation: Retailers buy goods and sell them in smaller quantities that are convenient for consumers.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse trading activities in the community.

questions.prompt: Which example shows a service rather than a good?
options: A haircut at a barber shop
A loaf of bread
A pair of shoes
A packet of milk
questions.correctAnswer: A haircut at a barber shop
questions.explanation: A service is an activity done for someone. It cannot be stored or touched in the same way as a physical good.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between goods and services found in the market.

questions.prompt: Which statement about goods is true?
options: Goods are tangible items that can usually be touched or stored
Goods are always invisible activities
Goods cannot be moved from one place to another
Goods are the same as promises only
questions.correctAnswer: Goods are tangible items that can usually be touched or stored
questions.explanation: Goods are physical items such as books, maize flour, clothes, and furniture.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse types and importance of goods and services found in the local market.

questions.prompt: Why are goods and services important to consumers?
options: They help satisfy human needs and wants
They make scarcity disappear completely
They stop all buying decisions
They remove the need for work
questions.correctAnswer: They help satisfy human needs and wants
questions.explanation: Consumers use goods and services to meet needs such as food, shelter, learning, transport, and communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Embrace the value of goods and services for the satisfaction of human wants.

questions.prompt: Where may a consumer buy goods and services in a Kenyan community?
options: Open-air markets, kiosks, supermarkets, service shops, or online platforms
Only inside a classroom cupboard
Only from traffic signs
Only from a closed office with no seller
questions.correctAnswer: Open-air markets, kiosks, supermarkets, service shops, or online platforms
questions.explanation: Consumers can obtain goods and services from physical markets, shops, service providers, and digital platforms.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sources and places where consumers may buy goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches a good and a service?
options: Book and transport
Haircut and banking
Bread and shoes
Teaching and repair work
questions.correctAnswer: Book and transport
questions.explanation: A book is a tangible good, while transport is an activity provided as a service.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between goods and services found in the market.

questions.prompt: Which feature makes services different from most goods?
options: Services are usually performed and cannot be stored for later use
Services are always counted in kilograms
Services can always be touched and packed
Services never involve people
questions.correctAnswer: Services are usually performed and cannot be stored for later use
questions.explanation: A service such as teaching, repair, or transport is an activity performed for a customer and is not stored like a product.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse characteristics of goods and services found in the local market.

questions.prompt: What are economic resources?
options: Inputs used to produce goods and services
Only finished products in a shop
Receipts kept after buying items
Rules for spelling business words
questions.correctAnswer: Inputs used to produce goods and services
questions.explanation: Economic resources include land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship used in production.
questions.learningOutcome: Examine the characteristics of economic resources used for production of goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which list contains factors of production?
options: Land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship
Rainbows, songs, games, and jokes
Receipts, stamps, posters, and bells
Wants, dreams, guesses, and rumours
questions.correctAnswer: Land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship
questions.explanation: The main factors of production are natural resources, human effort, man-made tools or money, and enterprise organisation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse types of economic resources in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which example represents labour as an economic resource?
options: A tailor sewing school uniforms
A sewing machine in a workshop
Cotton growing on a farm
A business idea written in a notebook
questions.correctAnswer: A tailor sewing school uniforms
questions.explanation: Labour is the human effort, skill, and time used in producing goods or providing services.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse types of economic resources in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which action shows sustainable use of economic resources?
options: Planting tree seedlings after harvesting trees for timber
Dumping waste into a river
Using soil without preventing erosion
Breaking tools after every project
questions.correctAnswer: Planting tree seedlings after harvesting trees for timber
questions.explanation: Sustainable use protects resources so they can continue supporting production and community needs in future.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore sustainable ways of using economic resources in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Why is resource mapping useful in a local community?
options: It helps identify and classify resources available for production
It hides all useful materials from learners
It proves that every resource is unlimited
It replaces communication in business
questions.correctAnswer: It helps identify and classify resources available for production
questions.explanation: Resource mapping shows what resources exist, where they are found, and how they can support production responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Conduct resource mapping in the local community and classify economic resources.

questions.prompt: Which option classifies a tractor used on a farm?
options: Capital
Labour
Land
Entrepreneurship
questions.correctAnswer: Capital
questions.explanation: Capital includes tools, machines, buildings, and money used to support production.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify economic resources used in production.

questions.prompt: Which statement best shows the importance of economic resources?
options: They are used to create goods and services that satisfy needs and wants
They prevent all enterprise activity
They make consumers stop choosing
They are useful only when wasted
questions.correctAnswer: They are used to create goods and services that satisfy needs and wants
questions.explanation: Economic resources are important because production depends on them to meet consumer and community needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the importance of economic resources in Kenya for the production of goods and services.

questions.prompt: What is communication in business?
options: The process of passing information between people or organisations
The process of hiding all prices from customers
The process of making goods without workers
The process of ignoring customer feedback
questions.correctAnswer: The process of passing information between people or organisations
questions.explanation: Business communication allows sellers, buyers, workers, and suppliers to share information clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Assess the meaning and importance of communication in business.

questions.prompt: Why is clear communication important in a business?
options: It helps avoid mistakes, delays, and misunderstandings
It ensures customers never ask questions
It hides product information
It stops workers from cooperating
questions.correctAnswer: It helps avoid mistakes, delays, and misunderstandings
questions.explanation: Clear communication helps orders, prices, complaints, and instructions to be understood accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the role of effective communication in business.

questions.prompt: Which ICT tool can a business use to send a price list quickly to customers?
options: Email or messaging application
Hand hoe only
Watering can only
Blank receipt book
questions.correctAnswer: Email or messaging application
questions.explanation: Digital communication tools can share information quickly with customers, suppliers, and workers.
questions.learningOutcome: Use ICT tools in business communication.

questions.prompt: A customer complains that a delivered chair is broken. Which response shows effective business communication?
options: Listen politely, record the complaint, and explain the next step
Ignore the customer and close the shop
Laugh at the complaint
Delete all transaction records
questions.correctAnswer: Listen politely, record the complaint, and explain the next step
questions.explanation: Effective communication is respectful, clear, and useful for solving business problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the role of effective communication in business.

questions.prompt: Which message is most suitable for confirming a customer's order?
options: Your order is for 10 notebooks at 50 shillings each, to be collected today at 4 p.m.
Maybe something is somewhere later
Come if you want anything
The price is a secret
questions.correctAnswer: Your order is for 10 notebooks at 50 shillings each, to be collected today at 4 p.m.
questions.explanation: A useful business message gives specific details about quantity, price, place, and time.
questions.learningOutcome: Use ICT tools in business communication.

questions.prompt: Which communication practice protects trust when advertising a product online?
options: Giving truthful details about price, quality, and delivery
Using fake pictures to attract buyers
Hiding extra charges until payment
Promising goods that are not available
questions.correctAnswer: Giving truthful details about price, quality, and delivery
questions.explanation: Honest communication helps customers make informed choices and protects a business reputation.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the role of effective communication in business.

questions.prompt: What is production in business?
options: Creating goods and services or increasing their usefulness
Destroying useful resources for fun
Keeping products away from consumers forever
Writing a shopping list only
questions.correctAnswer: Creating goods and services or increasing their usefulness
questions.explanation: Production involves making goods, providing services, or adding value so that needs and wants can be satisfied.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore the meaning and importance of production in the community.

questions.prompt: Which activity adds value through production?
options: Turning wheat flour into bread for sale
Leaving maize to rot in a store
Throwing away usable timber
Refusing to repair tools
questions.correctAnswer: Turning wheat flour into bread for sale
questions.explanation: Changing raw materials into useful products adds value and creates goods consumers can buy.
questions.learningOutcome: Explore the meaning and importance of production in the community.

questions.prompt: Which reward is usually linked to labour as a factor of production?
options: Wages or salary
Rent
Interest
Profit
questions.correctAnswer: Wages or salary
questions.explanation: Labour provides human effort and is commonly rewarded through wages or salary.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the importance, characteristics, and rewards for the factors of production.

questions.prompt: Which reward is usually linked to land as a factor of production?
options: Rent
Wages
Profit
Commission only
questions.correctAnswer: Rent
questions.explanation: Land and natural resources are commonly rewarded through rent when they are used in production.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the importance, characteristics, and rewards for the factors of production.

questions.prompt: A consumer says maize flour packets are underweight. Which consumer concern is being raised?
options: Quantity
Colour of the shop wall
Name of the delivery bicycle
Size of the seller's notebook
questions.correctAnswer: Quantity
questions.explanation: Quantity concerns arise when consumers question the amount, weight, or measure of goods supplied.
questions.learningOutcome: Examine consumer concerns to be addressed in the production of goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which production decision best protects consumer safety?
options: Using clean equipment and clearly labelling ingredients
Hiding expiry dates
Mixing food with unsafe substances
Ignoring hygiene during packaging
questions.correctAnswer: Using clean equipment and clearly labelling ingredients
questions.explanation: Safe production protects consumers by maintaining hygiene, quality, accurate labels, and proper handling.
questions.learningOutcome: Examine consumer concerns to be addressed in the production of goods and services.

questions.prompt: Why is entrepreneurship important in production?
options: It organises other resources and takes business risks
It replaces all workers with no planning
It makes land unnecessary forever
It prevents goods from reaching customers
questions.correctAnswer: It organises other resources and takes business risks
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur combines land, labour, and capital to produce goods or services and accepts business risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the importance, characteristics, and rewards for the factors of production.

questions.prompt: A school club makes reusable bags from old fabric. Which value of production is shown?
options: Creating useful goods while using resources responsibly
Wasting all resources quickly
Stopping consumers from getting goods
Avoiding any skill development
questions.correctAnswer: Creating useful goods while using resources responsibly
questions.explanation: Production can satisfy wants, build skills, create income, and encourage responsible use of resources.
questions.learningOutcome: Embrace the value of factors of production in producing goods and services to satisfy human wants.

questions.prompt: What is a market in Business Studies?
options: A place or arrangement where buyers and sellers exchange goods or services
Only a building with a red roof
A list of tax penalties
A locked cupboard with no customers
questions.correctAnswer: A place or arrangement where buyers and sellers exchange goods or services
questions.explanation: A market may be physical or digital as long as buyers and sellers can exchange goods or services.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate the terms market, marketing, and consumer to the consumption and business environment.

questions.prompt: What is marketing?
options: Activities used to inform, attract, and satisfy customers for goods or services
A method of hiding products from buyers
The act of paying tax only
A way of avoiding customer needs
questions.correctAnswer: Activities used to inform, attract, and satisfy customers for goods or services
questions.explanation: Marketing connects products with consumers through information, pricing, place, promotion, and customer care.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate the terms market, marketing, and consumer to the consumption and business environment.

questions.prompt: Which factor should a trader consider when choosing a market for fresh mangoes?
options: Presence of customers, transport, storage, and likely demand
Only the colour of the trader's pen
Whether customers dislike fruit
How to hide the mangoes from buyers
questions.correctAnswer: Presence of customers, transport, storage, and likely demand
questions.explanation: A suitable market depends on demand, access, transport, storage needs, competition, and customer ability to buy.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors considered when selecting a suitable market for goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which ICT platform can be used to market goods and services?
options: A business social media page
A broken calculator
A closed notebook with no contacts
A silent classroom wall with no message
questions.correctAnswer: A business social media page
questions.explanation: Social media, websites, and messaging platforms can help a business share product information with customers.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ICT platforms used for marketing goods and services.

questions.prompt: Why should a seller understand consumer needs before marketing?
options: To offer goods or services that customers are likely to value
To force every customer to buy the same item
To avoid quality improvement
To make all prices secret
questions.correctAnswer: To offer goods or services that customers are likely to value
questions.explanation: Marketing works better when a seller understands what consumers need, can afford, and prefer.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the role of marketing in the satisfaction of human needs and wants in society.

questions.prompt: Which advertisement is most responsible for a Grade 7 school club selling notebooks?
options: Durable 96-page notebooks, 60 shillings each, available at the club table on Friday
Magic notebooks guarantee top marks for everyone
Buy today or your friends will reject you
The price is hidden until after payment
questions.correctAnswer: Durable 96-page notebooks, 60 shillings each, available at the club table on Friday
questions.explanation: Responsible marketing gives truthful information about product features, price, place, and time.
questions.learningOutcome: Use appropriate marketing information to support consumer choice.

questions.prompt: Why may a business use both a physical shop and an online page?
options: To reach customers who prefer different buying channels
To confuse every buyer
To avoid sharing product information
To stop all sales records
questions.correctAnswer: To reach customers who prefer different buying channels
questions.explanation: Using more than one market channel can help a business reach different consumers conveniently.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ICT platforms used for marketing goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which situation best shows government involvement in business?
options: A county office issuing a business permit to a shop owner
A learner sharpening a pencil
A customer choosing a snack flavour
A shopkeeper arranging shelves by colour only
questions.correctAnswer: A county office issuing a business permit to a shop owner
questions.explanation: Government gets involved in business through regulation, licensing, consumer protection, taxation, and support services.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Justify the need for government involvement in business in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Why does the government regulate business activities?
options: To protect consumers, ensure fair trade, collect revenue, and support development
To stop every legal business from operating
To make all prices secret
To prevent people from working honestly
questions.correctAnswer: To protect consumers, ensure fair trade, collect revenue, and support development
questions.explanation: Government regulation helps businesses operate lawfully while protecting consumers and the wider economy.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the role of Government in business in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which document is commonly needed to start and operate a simple business legally in Kenya?
options: Business permit or licence
Sports certificate only
Birthday card
Blank drawing paper
questions.correctAnswer: Business permit or licence
questions.explanation: A business permit or licence shows that a business has been allowed to operate by the relevant authority.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the legal requirements for starting and operating a simple business in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which business is most likely to require attention to public health rules?
options: A food kiosk selling cooked meals
A learner reading a storybook
A person walking to school
A football fan watching a match
questions.correctAnswer: A food kiosk selling cooked meals
questions.explanation: Businesses handling food must observe hygiene and health requirements to protect customers.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Identify legal requirements for starting and operating a simple business in Kenya.

questions.prompt: A trader uses a weighing scale that gives customers less maize than they pay for. Why may government action be needed?
options: To protect consumers from unfair business practices
To reward dishonest measurement
To stop customers from buying maize
To remove all market competition
questions.correctAnswer: To protect consumers from unfair business practices
questions.explanation: Government agencies can enforce fair trade rules so that consumers receive the quantity and quality they pay for.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Justify the need for government involvement in business in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which government role can help small traders improve their businesses?
options: Providing training, advice, and business support services
Encouraging fake products
Banning all record keeping
Making roads unusable
questions.correctAnswer: Providing training, advice, and business support services
questions.explanation: Training and advisory services can help traders improve planning, quality, records, and customer service.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the role of Government in business in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which action should a learner recommend before opening a small food business near school?
options: Find out the required permits, hygiene rules, and safe food handling practices
Start secretly without asking about rules
Ignore customer safety
Avoid keeping any records
questions.correctAnswer: Find out the required permits, hygiene rules, and safe food handling practices
questions.explanation: A responsible business owner checks legal and health requirements before starting operations.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Identify legal requirements for starting and operating a simple business in Kenya.

questions.prompt: What is a tax?
options: Money paid to government to fund public services and development
A free gift paid only to shops
A product sold in a market stall
A school club membership badge
questions.correctAnswer: Money paid to government to fund public services and development
questions.explanation: Taxes are compulsory payments made to government so it can provide services and manage public responsibilities.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of tax and taxation in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains taxation?
options: The process by which government collects taxes from people and businesses
The process of hiding money from public records
The process of giving goods away without records
The process of avoiding all public services
questions.correctAnswer: The process by which government collects taxes from people and businesses
questions.explanation: Taxation is the system government uses to collect revenue for public needs such as roads, schools, health, and security.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of tax and taxation in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Why is paying taxes important to Kenya?
options: Taxes help fund public goods and services such as roads, hospitals, and schools
Taxes stop all development projects
Taxes are used only to close markets
Taxes make record keeping unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Taxes help fund public goods and services such as roads, hospitals, and schools
questions.explanation: Tax revenue supports public services and infrastructure that benefit citizens and businesses.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Examine the importance of paying taxes in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which value is shown by a trader who honestly files tax information?
options: Integrity
Carelessness
Dishonesty
Wastefulness
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity
questions.explanation: Honest tax compliance shows integrity, responsibility, and citizenship.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Desire to pay taxes as a Kenyan citizen.

questions.prompt: A community wants a new bridge to improve access to markets. How can taxes support this need?
options: Government can use tax revenue to build and maintain public infrastructure
Taxes can make rivers disappear
Taxes stop traders from transporting goods
Taxes replace the need for planning
questions.correctAnswer: Government can use tax revenue to build and maintain public infrastructure
questions.explanation: Tax money can finance infrastructure that helps people move, trade, learn, and access services.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Investigate the need for paying taxes in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which poster message would best encourage responsible tax payment?
options: Pay taxes honestly to support public services and national development
Hide taxes to stop roads from being built
Taxes are only for people you dislike
Public services do not need funding
questions.correctAnswer: Pay taxes honestly to support public services and national development
questions.explanation: A good civic message connects tax payment with services, development, honesty, and responsibility.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Sensitise the school community on the importance of paying taxes.

questions.prompt: Which situation shows a direct benefit of tax-funded services to business?
options: A maintained road helps farmers take produce to market
A broken bridge stops all trade
A dark street prevents customers from visiting
A closed clinic makes workers less healthy
questions.correctAnswer: A maintained road helps farmers take produce to market
questions.explanation: Public infrastructure funded by revenue can lower transport difficulty and support business activity.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Examine the importance of paying taxes in Kenya.

questions.prompt: What is a business transaction?
options: An exchange or event involving money, goods, or services in business
A sports practice timetable
A weather condition in the morning
A song performed at assembly
questions.correctAnswer: An exchange or event involving money, goods, or services in business
questions.explanation: Business transactions include buying, selling, paying, receiving, borrowing, and other events that affect business records.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of a business transaction as used in business.

questions.prompt: Which example is a business transaction?
options: A shop sells two pens and receives 40 shillings
A learner watches clouds moving
A school bell rings at lunch time
A tree grows beside a classroom
questions.correctAnswer: A shop sells two pens and receives 40 shillings
questions.explanation: The sale changes the shop's goods and cash position, so it is a business transaction.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of a business transaction as used in business.

questions.prompt: What is a cash transaction?
options: A transaction paid for immediately
A transaction paid for after many months only
A transaction with no buyer or seller
A transaction that cannot be recorded
questions.correctAnswer: A transaction paid for immediately
questions.explanation: In a cash transaction, payment is made at the time the goods or services are provided.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between cash and credit transactions in business.

questions.prompt: What is a credit transaction?
options: A transaction where payment is made later
A transaction that has no price
A transaction that avoids records
A transaction paid only with coins immediately
questions.correctAnswer: A transaction where payment is made later
questions.explanation: In a credit transaction, goods or services are supplied first and payment is expected at an agreed future time.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between cash and credit transactions in business.

questions.prompt: Which document is commonly issued to show that payment has been received?
options: Receipt
Invitation card
Weather chart
Sports score sheet
questions.correctAnswer: Receipt
questions.explanation: A receipt provides evidence that payment has been made and received.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify financial documents used in buying and selling in business.

questions.prompt: Which financial document asks a buyer to pay for goods or services supplied?
options: Invoice
Storybook
Bus map
Class register
questions.correctAnswer: Invoice
questions.explanation: An invoice lists goods or services supplied, amounts charged, and the total the buyer should pay.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify financial documents used in buying and selling in business.

questions.prompt: Why should a business keep financial documents?
options: They provide evidence for records, decisions, and follow-up
They make all money disappear
They stop customers from buying
They replace the need to deliver goods
questions.correctAnswer: They provide evidence for records, decisions, and follow-up
questions.explanation: Financial documents help a business remember transactions, settle disputes, and prepare accurate records.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the role of financial documents in record keeping in business.

questions.prompt: Which method can be used to make payment for goods and services?
options: Mobile money transfer
A blank poster only
A rumour from a friend
A weather forecast
questions.correctAnswer: Mobile money transfer
questions.explanation: Payments can be made using cash, mobile money, bank transfer, cards, cheques, or other accepted methods.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse methods used in making payments for goods and services.

questions.prompt: A customer pays for vegetables using mobile money and receives a message. Why is the message useful?
options: It can support proof that payment was made
It makes the vegetables grow again
It replaces the need to count goods
It hides the amount paid forever
questions.correctAnswer: It can support proof that payment was made
questions.explanation: Payment confirmation messages help both buyer and seller verify the transaction details.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse methods used in making payments for goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which transaction is a credit transaction?
options: A shop supplies flour today and the hotel agrees to pay next Friday
A customer pays cash before leaving the shop
A learner pays fare immediately
A buyer pays with mobile money at once
questions.correctAnswer: A shop supplies flour today and the hotel agrees to pay next Friday
questions.explanation: The buyer receives goods now and pays later, so the transaction is on credit.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between cash and credit transactions in business.

questions.prompt: A buyer orders 20 exercise books from a supplier. Which document may the buyer send first?
options: Purchase order
Receipt for payment not yet made
Weather report
Talent show programme
questions.correctAnswer: Purchase order
questions.explanation: A purchase order states the goods a buyer wants to buy before the supplier delivers them.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify financial documents used in buying and selling in business.

questions.prompt: Which detail should appear on a simple receipt?
options: Date, amount paid, item bought, and seller details
Only a drawing of a flower
Only the buyer's favourite colour
Only a blank signature space
questions.correctAnswer: Date, amount paid, item bought, and seller details
questions.explanation: A useful receipt records transaction details that can later prove what was bought, when, from whom, and for how much.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify financial documents used in buying and selling in business.

questions.prompt: Which action best protects a business after receiving payment by mobile money?
options: Confirm the transaction details and record the sale
Delete the message before checking it
Give goods without confirming the amount
Refuse to keep any record
questions.correctAnswer: Confirm the transaction details and record the sale
questions.explanation: Checking and recording payment details reduces mistakes and supports reliable financial records.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse methods used in making payments for goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which transaction record would best help resolve a dispute about goods delivered on credit?
options: An invoice and delivery note showing quantities and dates
A blank exercise page
A song title from assembly
A market rumour
questions.correctAnswer: An invoice and delivery note showing quantities and dates
questions.explanation: Documents showing what was supplied, when, and at what price help both parties verify the transaction.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the role of financial documents in record keeping in business.

questions.prompt: A shopkeeper sells goods worth 750 shillings on credit. Which record should be updated?
options: A debtor or credit sales record
A weather observation table
A football fixture list
A personal birthday calendar only
questions.correctAnswer: A debtor or credit sales record
questions.explanation: Credit sales should be recorded so the business can follow up payment from the customer.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between cash and credit transactions in business.

questions.prompt: A learner has 500 shillings and wants a maths set, snacks, a storybook, and data bundles. Which first step best supports wise choice?
options: Rank the items by importance and compare them with available money
Buy the first item seen at the kiosk
Spend all the money on snacks
Avoid thinking about needs and wants
questions.correctAnswer: Rank the items by importance and compare them with available money
questions.explanation: Ranking choices against limited money applies scale of preference and helps satisfy the most important needs first.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare a scale of preference to satisfy personal needs and wants.

questions.prompt: A group project has old fabric, two sewing needles, skilled learners, and a teacher mentor. Which resource is entrepreneurship?
options: The learner who organises the idea, resources, and selling plan
The old fabric
The sewing needles
The classroom floor
questions.correctAnswer: The learner who organises the idea, resources, and selling plan
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship is the ability to organise resources, identify an opportunity, and take responsibility for the business risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify economic resources used in production.

questions.prompt: A small bakery receives complaints about high prices, small loaf sizes, and unclear ingredients. Which response best addresses consumer concerns?
options: Review pricing, standardise loaf weight, and label ingredients clearly
Ignore the complaints and reduce quality further
Hide weighing scales from customers
Stop keeping production records
questions.correctAnswer: Review pricing, standardise loaf weight, and label ingredients clearly
questions.explanation: Consumer concerns about price, quantity, and ingredients should be addressed through fairness, quality control, and clear information.
questions.learningOutcome: Examine consumer concerns to be addressed in the production of goods and services.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to sell handmade cards online and at school. Which marketing plan is most suitable?
options: Show clear photos, state prices, identify target customers, and arrange safe delivery or collection
Post unclear photos and hide the price
Promise delivery without making the cards
Advertise only to people who do not need cards
questions.correctAnswer: Show clear photos, state prices, identify target customers, and arrange safe delivery or collection
questions.explanation: A good marketing plan gives truthful product information, chooses a suitable market, and makes buying convenient.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors considered when selecting a suitable market for goods and services.

questions.prompt: Which decision best combines talent, ethics, and income generation?
options: Use drawing skill to design original labels for local products at an agreed price
Copy another artist's logo and sell it secretly
Promise designs without doing the work
Overcharge customers after agreeing on a lower price
questions.correctAnswer: Use drawing skill to design original labels for local products at an agreed price
questions.explanation: Ethical income generation uses talent honestly, respects other people's work, and honours agreements.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ethical issues related to the use of talents and abilities in business.

questions.prompt: A school club sells seedlings and wants to keep accurate records. Which document set is most useful?
options: Receipts for sales, purchase records for inputs, and a cash summary
Only photos of learners smiling
Only a list of favourite tree names
A blank poster with no figures
questions.correctAnswer: Receipts for sales, purchase records for inputs, and a cash summary
questions.explanation: Sales, purchases, and cash summaries help the club track income, expenses, stock, and accountability.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the role of financial documents in record keeping in business.

questions.prompt: A market trader pays taxes, keeps receipts, uses fair measures, and renews a permit. Which conclusion is best?
options: The trader is supporting lawful and responsible business practice
The trader is avoiding all government involvement
The trader is refusing consumer protection
The trader is making records useless
questions.correctAnswer: The trader is supporting lawful and responsible business practice
questions.explanation: Compliance with tax, permits, fair measurement, and records supports trust, consumer protection, and legal operation.
questions.strandTitle: Government and Global Influence in Business
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the role of Government in business in Kenya.

questions.prompt: A learner is asked to design a simple school project that uses business knowledge to solve a need. Which plan is strongest?
options: Survey needs, choose one need, map resources, set a budget, sell or provide the solution, and review records
Choose a random idea and spend money without records
Ignore available resources and copy another school blindly
Start selling before knowing the need or cost
questions.correctAnswer: Survey needs, choose one need, map resources, set a budget, sell or provide the solution, and review records
questions.explanation: A strong project uses research, prioritising, resource mapping, budgeting, action, and reflection to solve a real need responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply business knowledge to address an identified need in the school community.
